instructions: 1. Run workflow:set-up-a-business-on-trillion first (or make record:business-setup:facts with business_name, owner_name, seller_return_url and channels); this workflow stops with "facts row missing" without it.
2. Make sure the offers are rows of type record:offer in your records with price options in whole cents (for example Member 4000 cents a month, Session 60000 cents one time).
3. Say "Run workflow:take-payments-with-stripe". Step set-up-payment-links makes one payment link per price option (a free offer gets none) and is safe to run again: it finds the links it made.

4. Open one link in Stripe test mode and pay with Stripe's published test card, then tell your AI the test purchase was made; it finds the completed checkout and compares the last 7 days of money events to the checkouts.

5. If an offer pays another seller (facts.payee_account_ref), step pay-a-third-seller starts that checkout; otherwise it answers Not applicable. The last step ticks the payments row in list:business-setup-checklist and writes any gap to list:business-setup-gaps.

worked_examples.title: Two offers become two payment links, the member link returning to its own page
worked_examples.ask: Make payment links for the Member and Session offers.
worked_examples.given: From tools/take-payments/test/ensure-offer-payment-links.test.mjs ("every priced option gets a link carrying its offer and option, and free offers get none"): owner bakery-a, after_payment_url https://app.example/, offers Free (no price options), Member (offer:member, price:member-monthly, 4000 cents usd, subscription every month, post-purchase page /account?paid=1) and Session (offer:session, price:session, 60000 cents usd, one time).
worked_examples.hands_back: links ["offer:member / price:member-monthly", "offer:session / price:session"] (one link each, none for the Free offer): the Member link returns buyers to https://app.example/account?paid=1 and collects a card even on a trial, the Session link returns to https://app.example/ and creates a customer; each link carries metadata owner bakery-a, its offer_id and price_option_id. Running the step again finds the same links and makes no new ones; retired [].

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
